sources.title: Introducing Amazon Nova: A New Generation of Foundation Models
sources.evidence: December 3, 2024 announcement says Nova Micro, Lite and Pro are generally available that day; identifies Amazon as developer and Nova as the family.

sources.title: The Amazon Nova Family of Models: Technical Report and Model Card (March 2025 revision)
sources.evidence: Section 1.1 explicitly includes Micro among Transformer models; sections 2.2 and 2.3 establish function calling and 128k context. No total or active parameter count was found. Web extraction exceeded its size limit; retrieved full PDF with curl and inspected pdftotext output.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, and Premier - AWS AI Service Cards
sources.evidence: Service card scoped to April 30, 2025 specifies Micro text input/output and Transformer-based inference; discusses CoT prompting. It provides no Micro total/active counts or dense/MoE classification.

sources.title: Nova Micro - Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Current model card identifies amazon.nova-micro-v1:0, 128K context and client-side tool calling; describes speed/cost optimization for summarization, translation and classification. Its December 5, 2024 launch date conflicts with the earlier explicit GA announcement.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Premier: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: April 30, 2025 addendum references Micro as a distillation target but does not disclose its total or active parameter counts or architecture details.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation Models
sources.evidence: Later December 2025 family report checked for retrospective Micro specifications; no Micro entry or parameter disclosure appears in the searchable report.

sources.title: MASSIVE-Agents: A Benchmark for Multilingual Function-Calling in 52 Languages
sources.evidence: Later Amazon-authored comparison Table 1 has Nova Micro Params = NP, Max CL = 128k and release month 12/24. It supplies no numerical Micro count. Full PDF retrieved and Table 1 inspected via pdftotext after web text search failed.

sources.title: Complete request schema - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Micro is text-only; reasoningConfig is explicitly limited to Nova Pro and Nova Lite, excluding Micro. Schema includes toolConfig.

sources.title: Available foundation models - Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: Table dated July 29, 2026 lists Nova Micro / nova-textgeneration-micro with license AWS Service Terms. It appears beneath the Open-Weight Models heading, conflicting with explicit Nova proprietary-weight and escrow documentation.

sources.title: Iterative Training - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Explicitly calls Amazon Nova weights proprietary and says trained checkpoints stay in AWS-managed escrow buckets instead of being copied to customer accounts. Examples use Nova 2 Lite; Micro applicability is independently corroborated by s12.

sources.title: AWS Service Terms
sources.evidence: Section 50.1 includes Amazon Nova within AI Services; section 50.11 prohibits extracting or deriving model weights. Section 60.3.7 grants exclusive use of customized Nova models, without granting a public weight release.

sources.title: Customize Amazon Nova in Amazon SageMaker AI using Direct Preference Optimization
sources.evidence: July 23, 2025 tutorial specifically customizes Nova Micro (amazon.nova-micro-v1:0:128k); trained weights remain in Amazon-controlled escrow with special access controls. Customer manifests provide checkpoint paths for evaluation and Bedrock import.

sources.title: Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: AWS explicitly classifies Nova as a proprietary model family; this supports, but does not alone establish, weight-access status.

name.note: Official shortened model name; full branded name is Amazon Nova Micro.

developer.note: Developed by Amazon; technical report credited to Amazon AGI.

family.note: Nova is the first-party family; Micro is a variant, so normalize the baseline nova-micro family label.

release_date.note: Retain earliest public GA day explicitly announced by Amazon. Current Bedrock card says December 5; that later conflicting listing does not override December 3 availability.

open_weights.note: Explicit proprietary-weight statement, Micro-specific Amazon-controlled escrow, and extraction restrictions support false. The JumpStart table places Micro under Open-Weight Models, but its heading conflicts with more specific weight-access documentation; no public release/export is established by that placement.

license.note: First-party Micro row names these terms. This denotes service/customization terms, not a downloadable open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: No numerical total in the original revised report, service card or later Premier/Nova 2 reports checked. The later Amazon-authored comparison explicitly uses NP for Micro Params; do not infer size from benchmarks or hardware.

active_parameters_b.note: No separate active count disclosed in the checked primary sources. Transformer does not establish dense versus MoE or justify equating total and active parameters.

architecture.note: Explicit Transformer classification. Dense versus MoE and detailed configuration remain undisclosed in these sources.

context_window.note: 128K tokens in the Micro-specific card and 128k in report section 2.3, normalized to decimal tokens.

modalities.note: Micro accepts text and generates text; no image, video or audio capability is established.

reasoning.note: False for a dedicated API reasoning mode: the request schema limits reasoningConfig to Pro/Lite. Micro can still solve reasoning tasks and follow prompted CoT.

tool_call.note: Current card explicitly supports client-side tool calling; report evaluates Micro function calling.

description.value: Text-only Nova model for summarization, translation and classification, with a 128K-token context and tool calling.
description.note: Summary of documented inputs, output, context and tool calling without speed or price claims.

patch.description: Text-only Nova model for summarization, translation and classification, with a 128K-token context and tool calling.
patch.notes: Total and active parameter counts are not disclosed in checked primary reports; Transformer is confirmed, while dense versus MoE is unknown. Release uses Amazon’s December 3, 2024 GA announcement despite a December 5 date on the current Bedrock card. Micro remains proprietary under AWS Service Terms: customized weights stay in Amazon-controlled escrow; the JumpStart open-weight table heading conflicts with explicit weight-access documentation. Reasoning=false refers to a dedicated reasoning mode, not inability to perform reasoning tasks.

summary: Confirmed all 14 fields or their disclosure status. Correct family to nova, identify AWS Service Terms, add explicitly documented Transformer architecture, and tighten description. Preserve December 3, 2024 release, text-only 128K context, tool calling, and no dedicated reasoning mode. Parameters remain undisclosed after original and later primary-report/comparison checks. Resolve conflicting JumpStart open-weight grouping in favor of explicit proprietary-weight and Micro escrow evidence; preserve the conflict in notes.
